findings.title: Permission check uses && instead of ||, locking out team admins
findings.body: The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. With `&&`, a user has to be both a team admin AND a team owner to pass; team admins who are not owners are rejected, and the only way to be true is effectively to be an owner. The intent (matching `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` used elsewhere in the UI) is "admin OR owner", so this should be `||`. As written, team admins without ownership cannot add guests to a team booking, even though the UI lets them open the AddGuestsDialog.

findings.title: Case-sensitive attendee dedup creates duplicate attendees and emails
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` is filtered with `guest === attendee.email`, a strict (case-sensitive) equality against `booking.attendees[].email`. Submitting a guest email that differs only in case from an existing attendee (e.g. "John@Example.com" vs an existing "john@example.com") passes the filter, is inserted as a new attendee row, receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail, and is added to the calendar invite — producing a duplicate attendee and a duplicate confirmation for the same person. Compare emails with `guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase()` (or normalize both sides).

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive, allowing bypass via mixed case
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized with `.toLowerCase()`, but the `guest` value passed to `.includes(guest)` is the raw input. A blocked address can be submitted as e.g. "Bad@Email.com" and the check will miss it, so a blacklisted guest gets added to the booking and emailed. Normalize `guest` to lower case (or store a normalized form) before the includes check.

findings.title: Unbounded guests array is a DoS / abuse vector
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min` and no `.max`. Any authenticated user (organizer, attendee, or team owner) can submit a single mutation with thousands of emails; the handler will then create that many attendees, push them to the calendar via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and dispatch that many emails. There is no per-booking cap, no rate limit, and no per-user rate limit. Add a sensible `.max(...)` (e.g. 20-50) and reject larger payloads at the schema layer.

findings.title: Handler does not deduplicate the input array itself
findings.body: The filter only drops entries that collide with an existing attendee or that are blacklisted; it does not collapse duplicates within the submitted `guests` list. Submitting `["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` causes `createMany` to insert two attendee rows, send two confirmation emails, and add the same address twice to the calendar. Dedupe `guests` first (e.g. via `Array.from(new Set(guests.map(g => g.toLowerCase())))`) before filtering.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with original `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: After computing `uniqueGuests` (which drops duplicates vs. existing attendees and blacklisted entries), the handler still passes the original `guests` array to `sendAddGuestsEmails`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` the predicate `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` then misclassifies pre-existing attendees as "new" guests whenever the user resubmitted their email, sending them an unnecessary `AttendeeScheduledEmail` rather than the intended `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added addresses) instead.

findings.title: No transaction around attendee insert, calendar update, and emails
findings.body: The handler performs `prisma.booking.update` (inserts new attendees), then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, then `sendAddGuestsEmails` outside any transaction and without a workflow that compensates on failure. If the calendar call throws, the DB already has the new attendees but no email goes out. If the email send throws (the only step wrapped in try/catch), attendees are still committed and the calendar already has them. The whole flow should be wrapped in `prisma.$transaction` or, at minimum, the email send failure should surface a non-success result instead of being swallowed by `console.log`.

findings.title: Email-send failures are logged with console.log and otherwise swallowed
findings.body: The catch block does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and returns success. The caller (UI) gets a `Guests added` toast even though the notifications never went out, and the only trace is a `console.log` (which is typically not captured). Use `logger.error(...)` with the error and either return a non-success status or surface a partial-success warning to the organizer so they can re-trigger notifications.

findings.title: No check on booking status or end time; guests can be added to cancelled/past bookings
findings.body: The handler does not inspect `booking.status` or compare `booking.endTime` against the current time. The UI in `BookingListItem` still surfaces the "additional_guests" action on past and on cancelled bookings (the `bookedActions` array is shown for `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`, etc.), so an organizer (or attendee) can add new attendees and trigger `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to them for events that have already happened or were cancelled. Reject mutations when the booking is CANCELLED, REJECTED, or in the past (unless the event type explicitly allows it).

findings.title: Recurring event instances are not propagated to the series
findings.body: If the booking belongs to a recurring event, the new attendees are only added to this single `booking` row. The other instances of the series continue to point at the original attendee list, so a guest invited to one occurrence will not appear on the parent `recurringEventId`'s other instances. The original new-guests scheduling path (`handleNewBooking`/recurring helpers) handles this; this handler does not, and will leave the series inconsistent. Either add the guest to all future instances of the recurring series or restrict the action to non-recurring bookings and surface a clear error.

findings.title: Error toast builds string with undefined code and ignores fallback
findings.body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`; showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` — when `err.data` is missing, `err.data?.code` is the string "undefined", which is truthy, so the fallback to `unable_to_add_guests` never fires and the user sees "undefined: <key>". The error toast should fall back when either `code` or the translated message is missing/empty, and the rendered string should be cleaned up (e.g. only show the code when present).
